# Evidence: ICP for search

Strength scale, the folder's own (see `../README.md`):

- **Official**: a platform or a standard says it. A rule, not a result.
- **Measured**: a stated sample and method, not run by someone selling the thing measured.
- **Measured (vendor)**: a seller's own data with a stated sample. Trust the direction, not the size.
- **Survey**: people asked about themselves. The sign can be used; the size cannot.
- **Practice**: a named expert's method. Nobody measured it.
- **Untraced**: repeated widely, no source found, or the source does not say it.

Every source is in `sources.md`.

## What an ICP is

| Claim | Source | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| One ICP is a group for whom the value of solving the problem is roughly the same and who can be reached roughly the same way | Fuentes, via Lenny's Newsletter | Practice (one founder's post-mortem) |
| Segment first on the organisation (macro), then on the decision-making unit inside it (micro) | Wind and Cardozo 1974, via Choffray and Lilien 1980 p. 332 | Practice; primary unread, never tested |
| The macro stage is designed to run on secondary sources, without contact | Choffray and Lilien 1980 p. 332 | Practice (read in full) |
| A basis (why companies belong together) differs from a descriptor (an observable that predicts membership); descriptors are used for prediction only | Choffray and Lilien 1980 p. 331 | Practice (read in full) |
| A usable segment needs homogeneous response, enough size, and observable descriptors | Choffray and Lilien 1980 p. 331 | Practice |
| Go to the person level only when one message draws different responses from different people in one list | Kuipers thesis quoting Wind and Cardozo | Practice, weak chain (no primary read) |
| An ICP should not include qualification criteria | Kellogg, kellblog | Practice (assertion) |
| MEDDIC qualifies opportunities; created at PTC in 1996 | meddicc.com (commercially interested) | Practice; Highspot credits McMahon instead |
| No peer-reviewed or randomised evaluation exists for BANT, MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, CHAMP or SPICED | Search of the literature (this folder) | Measured (absence, as searched) |
| The earliest artefact called an Ideal Customer Profile is Miller-Heiman's five-criterion rubric, built by contrasting best and worst customers | The New Strategic Selling, via a third-party outline | Practice; book unread |
| One-to-many account programmes get ICPs; one-to-few get clusters and personas | ITSMA tiers (Burgess) | Practice |
| A profile built from second-hand data is a role-based profile, not a buyer persona | ITSMA, via Momentum ITSMA 2021 summary | Practice; 2017 post not found |
| Nests 1 and 2 (demographics, operating variables) are observable from outside; nests 3 to 5 need contact | Bonoma and Shapiro 1983, 1984 | Practice; HBR abstract only |
| Is the role part of the ICP: yes (Kellogg) against no (Gong, ITSMA, Wind and Cardozo) | Kellogg; Gong; ITSMA; Wind and Cardozo | Contested |

|---|---|---|
| A field must be observable, discriminating, actionable and filterable | Built on Mora Cortez et al. 2021 and Kotler's segment criteria | Practice (a synthesis) |
| An industry-label list (5,000 accounts) got 1% replies; rebuilt on the real capability (800 accounts), 27% | Agency operator | Practice; the agency did the work. Keep the mechanism, not the numbers |
| Profitability per period was highest for the early majority, not innovators | Adoption-stage literature (this folder) | Measured |
| The same company can be an early adopter of one innovation and a late adopter of another | Gartner ETA document | Official (the vendor's own definition) |
| Company size changed no dimension of the buying centre (31 firms, 62 purchases, 241 interviews) | Census study | Measured; contested by Pedeliento et al. 2019 |
| Firm size "clearly determines" end-user involvement | Pedeliento et al. 2019 | Measured |
| The size question needs more research | Cabanelas, Mora Cortez and Charterina 2023, IMM 108, 89 articles | Measured (review) |
| At 9 or more attributes, the 99th-percentile description matched nobody in 5 of 6 real datasets; 7 or more passed 0.3% in one dataset only | Chapman et al. 2008 | Measured (5 of 6 datasets consumer; random descriptions) |
| Observed against predicted prevalence r = 0.394 to 0.713 on survey data, 0.857 to 0.869 simulated | Chapman et al. 2008 | Measured |
| "About five" fields or personas | Miller-Heiman, ITSMA, Goodwin, converging | Practice, unmeasured |
| 70 to 100 data points per segmentation variable | Dolnicar, Grün, Leisch and Schmidt 2014 | Measured (simulation) |
| A persona cannot be falsified | Chapman and Milham 2006 | Practice (reasoned, peer reviewed) |
| B2B segmentation's financial impact "remains empirically unclear"; 67% of the literature is atheoretical | Mora Cortez et al. 2021 | Measured (review of 88 papers) |
| Neither founding framework has ever been tested | Mora Cortez et al. 2021 | Measured (absence) |
| Academic research on ABM is "virtually non-existent" | Cardinali, Mero, Severini and Terho 2024; IMM 133, 2026 | Measured (literature count) |
